exposure: increased cervical dilation at oxytocin initiation
cohort: The study included a representative sample of 7394 women who delivered in metropolitan France.
finding: Women frequently reported that perinatal professionals failed to seek consent for interventions during childbirth, with rates ranging from 36.6% to 60.2%, and specific maternal, obstetric, and organizational characteristics were associated with this lack of consent.
mod_finding: Lack of consent for emergency cesarean delivery was 36.6% and was associated with cesarean for fetal distress; delivery assisted by an obstetrician was more often associated with lack of consent for episiotomy.
cross-section timing: Data was collected at 2 months postpartum regarding childbirth experiences.
